headline: Wilderness Camping Permits and Fire Safety
reservation: Overnight stays in Wharton or Brendan T. Byrne State Forests require specific wilderness camping permits. These are managed through the NJ State Park Service and should be booked well in advance; check official sites for current campfire restrictions which change based on drought.

days.title: Iron and Glass History

stops.name: Batsto Village
stops.detail: Tour the restored 19th-century bog iron village and explore the historic Batsto Mansion.

stops.name: Atsion Mansion
stops.detail: Visit this Greek Revival landmark situated along the historic Mullica River route.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; forest roads are predominantly unpaved sand
days.note: Walking the village requires comfortable shoes as paths are sandy and uneven.

days.title: Tannin Waters and Cedar Swamps

stops.name: Wading River
stops.detail: Paddle the tea-colored waters through dense cedar stands and quiet pine forests.

stops.name: Apple Pie Hill
stops.detail: Visit Apple Pie Hill, but climb the fire tower only when NJDEP explicitly opens it to visitors; confirm access and hours beforehand.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for shuttle transfers and river access; conditions vary
days.note: River navigation can become difficult in late summer if water levels drop significantly.

days.title: Blueberry Bogs and Stunted Pines

stops.name: Whitesbog Village
stops.detail: Explore the birthplace of the cultivated blueberry amidst active cranberry bogs.

stops.name: Pygmy Forest
stops.detail: Observe the unique ecological anomaly of mature pitch pines that grow only chest-high.

days.driving: Allow 50 minutes; local farm roads are narrow but scenic
days.note: Whitesbog is a living history site; remain on trails to avoid disturbing active agricultural crops.

intel.title: Trailhead Access
intel.text: Main lots at Batsto and Whitesbog are paved, but small trailhead pull-offs are often loose sand. Ensure your vehicle is fully off the road to allow for emergency vehicle passage.

intel.title: Deep Barrens Blackout
intel.text: Expect total loss of cellular signal when traveling between Chatsworth and the Wading River. Carry a physical topographical map and compass if venturing off the main paved corridors.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel up in Hammonton, Pemberton, or Medford before entering the state forest interior. No fuel is available within the million-acre Pine Barrens core area.

intel.title: River Outfitter Windows
intel.text: Most canoe liveries operate on a strict morning shuttle schedule between 8 AM and 10 AM. Arrive early to complete waivers and secure your preferred river launch window.

intel.title: Sand Road Restrictions
intel.text: Internal forest roads are composed of deep, soft sand that can trap low-clearance vehicles. Stick to primary numbered routes unless you are experienced with regional sand driving.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Atlantic City International (ACY), rent a vehicle, and head to Hammonton for local produce and water supplies.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance SUV is strongly suggested for exploring interior sand roads; check rental terms for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Do not assume Apple Pie Hill fire tower is open at sunset; use only an explicitly authorized opening and its stated hours.
